text_en: For all people who were ignorant of God were foolish by nature; and they were unable from the good things that are seen to know the one who exists, nor did they recognize the artisan while paying heed to his works;
text_cn: 凡不认识天主的人，都是真正的愚人，因为，他们未能从看得见的美物，去发现那自有者；注意了工程，却不认识工程师；

text_en: but they supposed that either fire or wind or swift air, or the circle of the stars, or turbulent water, or the luminaries of heaven were the gods that rule the world.
text_cn: 反而认火、风、流动的空气、运转的星辰、洪流的巨涛、天上的光体，为统治世界的神。

text_en: If through delight in the beauty of these things people assumed them to be gods, let them know how much better than these is their Lord, for the author of beauty created them.
text_cn: 如果有人因这些东西的美丽而着迷，奉之为神；那么，他们就应知道：这些美物的主宰更是美丽，因为，全是美丽的唯一根源所创造的。

text_en: And if people were amazed at their power and working, let them perceive from them how much more powerful is the one who formed them.
text_cn: 如果有人惊奇这些东西的力量和效能，就应明白：创造这些东西的更有能力；

text_en: For from the greatness and beauty of created things comes a corresponding perception of their Creator.
text_cn: 因为，从受造物的伟大和美丽，人可以推想到这些东西的创造者。

text_en: Yet these people are little to be blamed, for perhaps they go astray while seeking God and desiring to find him.
text_cn: 不过，这种人的罪尚较轻微，因为，他们寻找天主，也有意找到，却一时误入了迷途；

text_en: For while they live among his works, they keep searching, and they trust in what they see, because the things that are seen are beautiful.
text_cn: 这或许是由于他们所见的世物实在美丽，因此在专务研究他的工程时，只追求外表；

text_en: Yet again, not even they are to be excused;
text_cn: 但他们仍然不能推辞无过：

text_en: for if they had the power to know so much that they could investigate the world, how did they fail to find sooner the Lord of these things?
text_cn: 因为他们既然能知道的如此渊博，甚至能探究宇宙，为什么不能及早发现这些东西的主宰？

text_en: But miserable, with their hopes set on dead things, are those who give the name “gods” to the works of human hands, gold and silver fashioned with skill, and likenesses of animals, or a useless stone, the work of an ancient hand.
text_cn: 有些人真是可怜！他们竟将希望寄于死东西上，竟称人的手工、金银和艺术的创作、动物的肖像、或古人雕刻的无用的石为神。

text_en: A skilled woodcutter may saw down a tree easy to handle and skillfully strip off all its bark, and then with pleasing workmanship make a useful vessel that serves life’s needs,
text_cn: 设想：有个木匠，锯来一棵适用的树木，精巧地剥净树皮，熟练地施展技巧，制成一件日常生活的用具；

text_en: and burn the cast-off pieces of his work to prepare his food, and eat his fill.
text_cn: 以后用工作剩余的碎木，煮饭充饥；

text_en: But a cast-off piece from among them, useful for nothing, a stick crooked and full of knots, he takes and carves with care in his leisure, and shapes it with skill gained in idleness; he forms it in the likeness of a human being,
text_cn: 后来由那些剩下一无所用的废木中，取出一块弯曲多疤的木头，在闲暇无事时，辛勤地加以雕刻，本着自己熟悉的手艺，按图样将它刻成一个人像，

text_en: or makes it like some worthless animal, giving it a coat of red paint and coloring its surface red and covering every blemish in it with paint;
text_cn: 或做成一个卑贱的兽像，涂上丹砂，将外皮漆成红色，遮住一切疤痕；

text_en: then he makes a suitable niche for it, and sets it in the wall, and fastens it there with iron.
text_cn: 随后，为它做一个适宜的居所，把它嵌在墙上，用钉子钉住，

text_en: He takes thought for it, so that it may not fall, because he knows that it cannot help itself, for it is only an image and has need of help.
text_cn: 预先加以照顾，免得它掉下来，因为他知道：这件东西是不能自助的，不过只是偶像，需要人来扶助。

text_en: When he prays about possessions and his marriage and children, he is not ashamed to address a lifeless thing.
text_cn: 但是，他反不感羞耻地向这无灵之物祷告，祈赐财富、妻室和子嗣；

text_en: For health he appeals to a thing that is weak; for life he prays to a thing that is dead; for aid he entreats a thing that is utterly inexperienced; for a prosperous journey, a thing that cannot take a step;
text_cn: 向这虚弱的东西，要求健康；向这死物，要求生命；向这无能的东西，要求援助；

text_en: for money-making and work and success with his hands he asks strength of a thing whose hands have no strength.
text_cn: 向这有脚不能行的东西，要求旅行；向这有手而毫无动作的东西，要求发财、工作、事业成功的力量。
